site_selection_index_test: suspicious oral mucosal lesions

site_selection_index_test: NR

index_test_type_transformed: Combined cytology and DNA image cytometry

site_selection_index_test: biopsies were taken from the area with most clinical suspicion (by inspection and palpation) of the pre-malignant or malignant lesion

technique: On local examination by inspection and palpation, the location, size of the lesion, the extent of local infiltration, oral hygiene, and cervical lymph node status were assessed.
positivity_threshold: clinically suspected to be premalignant or malignant
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: clinical suspicion of premalignant or malignant

site_selection_index_test: Oral rinse
technique: The technique of application involved rinsing of the mouth with water for 20 s to remove debris. Followed by application of 1% acetic acid for 20 s to remove ropey saliva. Then 1% toluidine blue oral rinse was given for 20 s. Again 1% acetic acid rinse was performed to remove mechanically retained stain. Finally, the mouth was rinsed with water.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that exhibited dark blue staining were deemed positive for premalignant or malignant tissue, while those with light staining or no color were considered negative
comments_index_test: There is a discrepancy in the manuscript regarding the concentration of the toluidine blue solution: the text states a 1% solution was used, whereas Figure 1 displays a '0.1% solution'.

site_selection_index_test: Patients above the age of 18 years with white or red and white oral lesions, suspicious of PMD
technique: Five percent acetic acid was applied to the lesion with a sterile disposable cotton applicator for 60 seconds.
positivity_threshold: The results of the acetic acid application were considered positive if the lesion appears opaque white (acetowhite) [Figures 1-3] and a negative if the lesion does not show any color change.

site_selection_index_test: Lesions from patients with suspected OPMDs and ulcerations suggestive of malignancy or nonhealing ulcers persisting for >2 weeks without any identifiable cause were included.
technique: First, a cotton tip was used to apply a 1% acetic acid solution to the lesions for 20 s to eliminate residue layers. Next, a 2x2 cm electrospun fiber patch containing 2% TB was applied to the lesion for 20 s. Finally, the mechanically retained stain was removed by applying 1% acetic acid using a cotton tip for 20 s.
positivity_threshold: positive (dark blue staining)

site_selection_index_test: clinically suspicious lesions
technique: Toluidine blue was applied with cotton bud for 10 to 20 seconds.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue was considered as positive for lesions suspicious of malignancy, light blue retention was considered as positive for premalignant lesions unless proved otherwise by biopsy, and lesion without retention was considered negative

site_selection_index_test: The main site of morphologically altered mucosa was selected
technique: 1%TB is applied in 4 steps; first, rinsing of oral cavity with water for 20 s to remove debris, then application or rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 s, after that application or rinse with TB solution (1% W/W) for 20 s and finally application or rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 s to eliminate mechanically retained stains.
positivity_threshold: A royal blue or a navy blue stain as shown in Fig. 1 was considered as a positive result even if either the entire lesion or a portion of the lesion is stained or stippled.
calibration_of_assessors: Dental surgeons in the selected institutions were trained by the expert in the field of Oral Medicine at their institutions. Live demonstrations of TB application were carried out to familiarise the procedure during the training programme.

site_selection_index_test: An oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, took pictures of the lesions, and picked the areas to be examined.
technique: For the application of toluidine blue, a cotton bud soaked in 1% acetic acid was used to clean the lesion prior to the application of toluidine blue with a different cotton tip for 30 s.
positivity_threshold: A positive lesion was the one which color changed to blue, while a negative lesion was with no change.
comments_index_test: The text mentions 33 patients received TB only and 24 received TB + vinegar (total 57), but the results table for TB reports 54 patients, suggesting 3 patients were excluded or unaccounted for.

index_test_arm_label: Combined Toluidine Blue and 5% Acetic Acid

site_selection_index_test: patients with the lesions in oral cavity having suspicion of malignancy were clinically selected.

positivity_threshold: lesions that showed dark blue staining were considered to be positive for premalignant or malignant tissue, while those with light staining, or totally not coloured, were considered negative.

site_selection_index_test: Applied directly on the lesion.
technique: Patients rinsed with 1% lactic acid and distilled water for 30 seconds. Target mucosa was dried with gauze. 1% MB dye was applied directly to the lesion with a cotton bud for 30 seconds. Patients then rinsed with 1% lactic acid for 30 seconds to remove excess dye.
positivity_threshold: Dark royal blue/deep blue stains of MB were considered as positive retention. Wide, shallow, faint, pale royal blue stains or no retention of the stain were considered as negative for MB retention.
comments_index_test: There is a discrepancy in the reported MB concentration: the Abstract reports 5% MB while the Methods section reports 1% MB.

index_test_arm_label: Methylene blue (MB) and Lugol's iodine (LI) double staining method

positivity_threshold: Lesions that displayed LOA were considered to be positive

site_selection_index_test: on oral lesions

blinding_index_test_examiner: Different examiners were involved in the screening and recruiting of patients, as well as the stain application technique, to prevent bias.
comments_index_test: Table 2 true positive, false negative, false positive, and true negative values sum to 34 for each index test, despite the study claiming to include 45 patients.

site_selection_index_test: OLBC using Orelcelx brush (Rovers Medical Devices, The Netherlands) was performed on each patient under local anesthesia before undergoing surgical biopsy
specimen_collection: Brush heads were preserved immediately into vials of methanol-based buffered preservative (ThinPrep PreservCyt, Hologic Inc, MA, USA) and transferred to a laboratory for processing.
technique: A liquid-based cytology (LBC) slide was automatically prepared for each OLBC sample using the standard protocol of the ThinPrep 2000 processor
positivity_threshold: NR

site_selection_index_test: Clinical examination of the patient's oral cavity was performed by an experienced head and neck surgeon (M.M., M.A.K., and H.A.E), followed by the acquisition of endoscopic multispectral autofluorescence images from both the suspicious oral lesion and a clinically healthy-appearing area in the corresponding contralateral anatomical side.
technique: The autofluorescence endoscopic images were acquired with a 10 mm circular field-of-view, ~ 100 μm lateral resolution, and < 3 s acquisition time per multispectral image.
positivity_threshold: the validation sample was classified as cancer/precancer if its predicted image-level score was greater than or equal to the optimized threshold, or as benign otherwise.

index_test_reagent_name: DNA mismatch repair proteins (MSH-6, MSH-2, MLH-1 and PMS-2)

site_selection_index_test: COE encompasses a manual and visual examination of intra- and extra-oral sites, following a complete clinical interview.
technique: Patients underwent a complete clinical interview followed by COE, a manual and visual examination of intra- and extra-oral sites; based on the clinical characteristics found, both examiners classified the lesions into benign or malignant.
positivity_threshold: Based on the clinical characteristics found, both the examiners classified the lesions into benign or malignant.
calibration_of_assessors: One of the two general dentists underwent a 1-year post-graduate training program in oral medicine at the Oral Medicine Unit, Federico II University of Naples, Italy, prior to performing COE and Vel-E.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Both examiners classified lesions and performed Vel-E on the basis of clinical information and in the absence of histological data, indicating blinding to the reference standard at the time of index test performance.
comments_index_test: COE was performed by two general dentists of differing experience levels (unskilled u-GD and skilled s-GD); results for each are reported separately in Table 2, but this row represents the COE test type overall (not split by examiner skill level).

site_selection_index_test: Both examiners classified oral lesions detected on clinical examination as benign or malignant and performed Vel-E on these same identified lesions
technique: The device was used, maintaining a distance of approximately 5 cm from the oral cavity to optimize the visualization of the natural tissue fluorescence and, if necessary, darken the operating theatre to reduce natural light and bring it to an acceptable level.
positivity_threshold: In the presence of LAF, the Vel-E is defined positive
calibration_of_assessors: One of the two general dentists underwent a 1-year post-graduate training program in oral medicine at the Oral Medicine Unit, Federico II University of Naples, prior to performing Vel-E, while the other examiner (u-GD) had no such specific training.
blinding_index_test_assessors: The examiners performed Vel-E on the basis of clinical information and in the absence of histological data, i.e., blinded to the reference standard result at the time of testing.
comments_index_test: Vel-E results were interpreted separately by an unskilled general dentist (u-GD) and a skilled/trained general dentist (s-GD); this row combines both examiners under the single VelScope arm since the anchor does not split by examiner, though the paper reports diagnostic accuracy separately for u-GD and s-GD.

index_test_commercial_name: GEMINI Medical Diagnostic System's (Changsha) DNA Image Cytometer (DNA-ICM)

positivity_threshold: Aneuploid group has more than 3 nuclei, or hyperdiploid group has 5% of total nuclei, or tetraploid group has 10% of total nuclei.

site_selection_index_test: oral cavity lesion or suspicious area

site_selection_index_test: NR

site_selection_index_test: Clinical examination of patients to identify suspected oral lesions

positivity_threshold: local, stipules and concentrated blue stains

technique: The lesions were photographed using IllumiScan in a dark room with maintained irradiation brightness at a distance of approximately 30 mm.

site_selection_index_test: The clinician selected the clinical lesion suspected of oral malignancy and scraped the entire lesion.

positivity_threshold: NR

site_selection_index_test: 10% formalin fixed biopsies, punch biopsy, incisional biopsy and excisional biopsies, measuring more than 1×1 cm in size
specimen_collection: left over formalin of specimen bottles in which the biopsy specimens were received
technique: The fixative fluid from the original specimen bottle was centrifuged at 3000 rpm for five min. The supernatant of the centrifuged material was discarded; and the sediments were washed two times in normal saline and used for smear preparation

calibration_of_assessors: Initially, 10 patients were examined to calibrate the visualization of colours for consistent assessment across the study.

site_selection_index_test: NR

site_selection_index_test: pathological sites, frequently from mucosal lesions and from other representative sites

positivity_threshold: NR

site_selection_index_test: Participants were screened for oral mucosal lesions, and those lesions were subjected to DrOroscope examination

positivity_threshold: loss of fluorescence in abnormal tissues, due to which the areas appear dark

positivity_threshold: Results categorized as 'doubtful', 'suspicious', and 'positive' were considered positive.

positivity_threshold: Results categorized as 'doubtful', 'suspicious', and 'positive' were summarized as 'tumour cell positive'.

site_selection_index_test: Patients with clearly visible oral lesions, which showed apparent variation from the normal healthy mucosa

positivity_threshold: cytology as negative (negative) and positive (doubtful, positive)

site_selection_index_test: clinically suspected OPMDS

positivity_threshold: 8 according to the Swede scoring system
comments_index_test: 25 patients were enrolled and received the index test. Table III indicates 2 patients missed biopsy, leaving 23 to be included in the diagnostic accuracy calculations for the Swede scoring system.
